title: 2050 'Weather Forecast' Predicts Crisis for Japan
paragraphs: What will the weather be like in Japan in 2050? A new video imagines a weather forecast from that year, and the picture it paints is worrying.

The video, called "2050 Weather Forecast (Ver. 2)," was released free online on August 3, 2026. It was produced by the 2050 Weather Forecast Production Committee, in which NHK Enterprises is one of the lead organizations, and it is supported by the United Nations in Japan. It is an updated version of a video made in September 2014 by NHK, Japan's national broadcaster, as part of a campaign by the World Meteorological Organization ahead of a United Nations climate summit. The new version features the same weather forecaster and climate scientist as the original, and it uses the latest scientific research.

The video imagines what Japan could look like in 2050 if current climate policies continue. In this scenario, days with temperatures of 40°C or higher could occur in as many as 157 locations across the country. As a result, people may face restrictions on outdoor activities. For example, children may be kept from playing outside, and outdoor construction work may be limited. The video also warns about more destructive "super typhoons."

In addition, the forecast shows how extreme heat and abnormal weather could affect agriculture and the food supply. In one example, a popular pork cutlet rice dish becomes a luxury item. Dr. Toshihiro Hasegawa, the president of the Japan International Research Center for Agricultural Sciences, advised on the food security issues in the video.
Worryingly, several of the scenarios in the 2014 video have already happened earlier than expected, including long periods of temperatures above 35°C.

However, the video also presents possible solutions, such as a faster switch to renewable energy and the wider use of electric vehicles. Its goal is to encourage stronger action on climate change. In a speech in June, UN Secretary-General António Guterres warned that the effects of climate change "are already here."
